message.content:
For a garden sculpture you’ll want a stone that can stand up to the elements while still offering good carving detail. **Granite** is usually the top choice for outdoor work because it’s hard, dense, and highly resistant to weathering, freeze‑thaw cycles, and biological growth. It also has a pleasing natural grain that can add visual interest.

If you’re looking for something softer that still holds up reasonably well, **marble** (especially Carrara or Calacatta) is excellent for finer detail and gives a classic look, though it can be more susceptible to acid rain and requires some maintenance. Other options include:

| Stone | Hardness | Weather Resistance | Typical Use |
|-------|----------|--------------------|-------------|
| Granite | 6–7 on Mohs | Very high | Outdoor monuments, garden statues |
| Marble | 3–5 | Moderate (acid‑resistant varieties better) | Indoor/Outdoor decorative pieces |
| Limestone | 2–4 | Low (weatherable) | Garden walls, low‑profile art |
| Sandstone | 2–6 | Variable | Landscape features, rustic sculptures |

So if durability and minimal upkeep are your priorities, granite is the most suitable rock for a garden sculpture.
